problem_statement.value: Hydraulic power steering on a 2019 work truck loses assist intermittently only when the ambient temperature is below 5C and the vehicle is parked on an incline overnight. Two competing explanations are both plausible: (a) the power-steering fluid viscosity rises so much that the variable-pressure regulator opens late, and (b) air trapped in the rack seal weeps in during the incline park and releases on first rotation. I want a mechanism that explains BOTH symptom patterns and a decisive experiment that separates them in one test. What is the mechanism, and what would kill each competing hypothesis?

desired_outcome.value: a single decisive bench test that separates the viscosity hypothesis from the air-weep hypothesis at under 200 USD
